steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the oranges, pineapple, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows and milk.
Mix together well and chill 1 hour before serving. Garnish with cherries.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Ambrosia Salad
raw_recipe.description: There 'll be twelve happy people at your table when you spoon us this delightful salad/dessert, made with Mandarin oranges, pineapple, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows and, of course, maraschino cherries.
raw_recipe.name: Coconut Ambrosia Salad

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the oranges, pineapple, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows and milk.
Mix together well and chill 1 hour before serving. Garnish with cherries.

review.reviewBody: I doubled the recipe and made this for thirty people at a baby shower - it was a huge hit! There were NO leftovers! I took the advice of many other reviewers added pecans and apples (with skins - and no celery!), added red and green grapes, strained the canned fruit overnight, added a large box of pistachio instant pudding to the whipped topping and no milk - made it very thick and creamy, not runny at all, and the colors of the fruit looked great - together it was a perfect combination! It was so simple. You can't go wrong with this recipe - add any fresh fruit you want (except raspberries or bananas - ask me how i know haha).

I did not put the milk & cherries in. I added the following: l large cottage cheese (small curd) 1 cup sour cream 1 cup crushed walnuts 1 pkg pistacchio jello Mixed well with electric mixer (this chops the oranges evenly)

Great salad. I followed other suggestions and substituted sour cream for the milk. I also added 1 cup of grapes and I used colored marshmallows. I went with pineapple tidbits instead of crushed and let the fruit drain for a few hours. I used 2 cups of sweetened shredded coconut but I found that it was maybe a little too much. Next time I will try 1 cup of coconut instead.

We liked this pretty well. We doubled the recipe for a big gathering. We made some slight changes based on the package sizes from our local grocery. We used 30 oz. mandarin oranges, 20 oz. crushed pineapple, 32 oz. whipped topping, 1 cup red grapes halved, 2 cups coconut shredded further in the food processer, 20 oz maraschino cherries. Use a very very big bowl if you doubled the recipe like I did. Reserve your juices and add some back before serving if you need it (I didn't).

I loved this recipe with the previously suggested additions: 1 cup chopped pecans, 1 diced green apple with skin on (both added a nice crunch and the apple helped cut sweetness), 1 (15 oz) can of fruit cocktail for more volume, 1 (3.4 oz) box of pistachio instant pudding, and I replaced the milk with 1/2 cup of sour cream. I'm glad I used unsweetened coconut flakes and I would try toasting them next time. The only part I'd change is I'd carefully monitor the ratio of whipped cream to fruit as I folded the cream in. I used 1 (8 oz) tub of whipped topping and my family felt it was too much. After draining the canned fruit I added it all together in a vegetable steamer which I'd placed inside a larger glass bowl. I sealed it and let the fruit continue draining overnight. This helped a lot.
This was a huge hit for our family. I did 1/2 cool whip, 1/2 sour cream, and about 1/2 cup of whipping cream instead of milk. I drained the fruit really well, and it didn't get watery.

Great recipe. I don’t use the additional milk unless I am using fresh whipped cream. The frozen whipped topping breaks down easy enough during mixing. I also refrigerate all ingredients overnight before mixing. You end up with a more solid salad. I hope you enjoy it as much as I do!

I made this for my husband for Father's Day dessert and it was a hit. Even my three year old wanted some. The only thing I did different was substituting cool whip with fresh heavy whipped cream (3/4 cup cream with about 1/4 cup sugar and 1/2 tsp vanilla). I also added a can of fruit cocktail. Overall, I adjusted the amount of the coconut and marshmallow to my desirable taste. Will definitely make this again for my next family gathering.
I made it as written and it was good but very sweet. I made it a second time with more fruit, and half the coconut and half the marshmallow.
Tasted great while making. My marshmallows were dried out.Oopsie, added extra milk and let them sit before adding the rest. This is a keeper.

I have made this salad for 30+ years with a few additions to my version. I skip the milk and use one can condensed milk, and one can cherry pie filling. This is such a popular salad everyone loves it and often is eaten as desert, skipping the pumpkin pie after dinner.
It’s kind of sweet, but on a hot summer day, it’s great.

Although I thought it was missing the fruit cocktail, I thought I would give it a try, due to I didnt have it. I will tell you I never missed it. No one did. I made exactly per the recipe. My family said I could make this weekly. hmmmm. You wont go wrong, give it a try.

@SweetStove… the whipped cream is 3.5 cups. “8 oz of whipped cream = 1 cup” you’re imagining is a VOLUME measurement. This is 8 oz weight, which is one whole tub. Be sure you measure it in cups (3.5) :)

Never made one before, no never liked it as well, but was asked to bring it for Christmas and it was delish! I double the pineapple and manderine oranges, 1 cup of cherries, added small pkg of pistachio pudding, about a half cup of half & half, grapes as well. YUM!
Not my thing but my aunt just commented this week about how good it was when I made it for a birthday party. That was 18 years ago!

I made this using the whole cans of pineapple and mandarin oranges, and no whipped topping, it is still very good I will add the whipped topping but have to go to store first. This is New Years Day so hope the store is open, if not the salad is still good and I will serve as is.

I absolutely love it, and my friends love it. Every year, I get invited to my friends for Thanksgiving. One time I thought I would make this recipe and bring it. Oh my gosh, everyone loved it. I have an open invitation along with other friends for Thanksgiving dinner at these friends house. Each year, when I ask them what they want me to bring, they say, "for sure, ambrosia salad!" I looked at some of the comments that others had made in adding different things. Each time, I do a little bit different, sometimes add milk, sometimes at sour cream, sometimes use pistachio pudding, or add different nuts, and even bananas! No matter what I do, everyone loves it! Thank you so much for this wonderful recipe and for making my friends happy!
I thought it was very good, light and refreshing. I substituted the maraschino cherries with fresh Mandarin oranges as a garnish on top. Loving It!!!
